correctness.rationale: The graph-2-packing criterion follows exactly from Kneser adjacency and common-neighbor cardinality n-2r+|A cap B|. For r>=11, a hypothetical four-block family needs at least 4r-12 > n coordinates, so degree at most three, with a concrete three-block witness. One/two coefficients are exact binomial counts. For each ordered admissible triple the eight disjoint Venn atoms have the stated nonnegative sizes, and the multinomial labeling count divided by six correctly counts unordered triples. The eight (k,t) profiles are distinct and exhaustive under coordinate permutations. The independent anchored-pair enumerator agrees for r=4..25; fully direct enumeration on K(9,4) agrees for all 2-/3-block families and orbit profiles. Infinite claims are proved symbolically, not inferred from finite checks.

originality.rationale: The new result is the all-cardinality enumerator and eight labeled-ground-set orbit sizes, not the previously known 2-packing maximum three. The 2023 Kneser paper explicitly gives the pairwise intersection criterion and scalar maximum; comparison with its detailed Section 4 shows no count of all 2-packings. Binary constant-weight code extremal bounds are an equivalent-language risk, but published general size tables do not determine the number of configurations. The 2010 classified codes have explicitly shorter parameter ranges; our n>=30 range starts beyond them. The 2006 length>=29 tables report code cardinality bounds and constructions rather than all packing-family counts. Bounded published-finding corpus searches returned no directly equivalent enumerator, though this is not proof of global novelty.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed Venn-atom formula or full code-family enumeration may imply the present factorial counts.
Full text of the 2010 code-classification paper was unavailable in current accessible checks; its explicitly stated parameter ranges do not overlap the claimed n>=30 interval.
Search nonappearance is not novelty proof; assessment is scoped to inspected claims and implication comparisons.

value.rationale: The theorem determines the complete independence/2-packing polynomial of the square of an infinite Kneser diagonal, and partitions all optimal configurations into exactly eight natural orbit types with explicit labeled multiplicities. These data are absent from the established scalar maximum-3 result and the coding-theoretic size tables; they quantify the full placement space of feasible mutually separated subsets. The formulas cover an unbounded range beyond the stated parameters of earlier finite code classifications. This is a natural complete family classification rather than an arbitrary finite slice or mere recomputation of the known scalar optimum.
